nativeReplayIssues.title: Historical Windows desktop tests failed on Unix-only libc CPU helper
nativeReplayIssues.body:
## Historical observation

The immutable replay of `cb95cf6d785c3073c192b95f0632cdae7b910894`
failed to compile desktop tests on Windows.
[Run 38842787230, job 116786450596](https://github.com/Aquaticats/Monochromatic/actions/runs/38842787230/job/116786450596)
ran the original package test task after its release build and release-command checks passed.
Rustc emitted `E0433: cannot find module or crate libc in this scope`
at `package/music-player/desktop-app/src/refresh_cost_tests.rs:99`, `:100`, and `:102`.
No test executed because the test binary did not compile.

The historical helper unconditionally calls `libc::getrusage`,
but `Cargo.toml` declares `libc` only on Linux and macOS.
The ignored benchmark still belongs to the compiled test module.
The separately missing Clippy component is a harness prerequisite issue.

## Existing resolution

Commit `2ec128bebf` added a Windows `GetProcessTimes` implementation and gated the Unix helper.
`doc/troubleshooting/music-player-windows-build-and-test.md`
already documents this exact historical failure and fix.
The newer immutable source `3434eaa455d569c18b52cf15100f77f9db251d21`
compiled successfully in [run 38844610546](https://github.com/Aquaticats/Monochromatic/actions/runs/38844610546)
on MSVC x64, MSVC ARM64, and GNU x64;
each nextest summary reports 1432 passed and one skipped.
The jobs still fail their separate preserved historical PowerShell assertion.

This issue records an already-fixed historical finding,
not a claim that the current source cannot compile on Windows.
The original failed replay remains part of the trial evidence.

nativeReplayIssues.body:
## Historical observation

The immutable source `cb95cf6d785c3073c192b95f0632cdae7b910894`
failed `change_plan::tests::random_edits_named_the_way_the_watcher_names_them_keep_the_queue_equal_to_the_walk`
on macOS Intel in
[run 38842787230, job 116786450062](https://github.com/Aquaticats/Monochromatic/actions/runs/38842787230/job/116786450062).
The assertion at `package/music-player/desktop-app/src/change_plan_tests.rs:58`
failed at seed 2, round 0.
The queue included `A/a/a2.mp3`,
while the filesystem walk returned `a/a/a2.mp3` with different ordering.
The historical generator deliberately samples both `a` and `A` without checking filesystem case behavior.

The run reported 54 passed, one failed, and one skipped;
1327 tests were not run because nextest stopped after the failure.
That incomplete execution is a separate harness recovery requirement.

Commit `95ec5a9da8` introduced `folder_names_ignore_case` and `pick_stem`
in `package/music-player/desktop-app/src/refresh_test_support.rs`
and used the helper for random tree names.
The helper probes the fixture filesystem rather than assuming behavior from the OS name.
`doc/troubleshooting/music-player-windows-build-and-test.md` documents this portability fix.

nativeReplayIssues.title: macOS rename watcher test rejects target reported under canonical path prefix
nativeReplayIssues.body:
## Observed failure

[Run 38843527788, job 116788771225](https://github.com/Aquaticats/Monochromatic/actions/runs/38843527788/job/116788771225)
ran unchanged source `3434eaa455d569c18b52cf15100f77f9db251d21` on macOS Intel.
Nextest failed `watch::tests::a_file_replaced_by_a_rename_is_reported_by_the_target_path`
at `package/music-player/desktop-app/src/watch_tests.rs:239`.

The test creates a temporary replacement and renames it over `a.flac`.
Its assertion requires the target path constructed from `std::env::temp_dir()`
to occur in the reported change set with the structural flag set.
The report contains `/private/var/folders/.../a.flac` and the temporary sibling,
both with the flag set;
the fixture path starts `/var/folders/...`.
The assertion reports `the target is named` despite the target filename being present under a different prefix.

The path identity mismatch is observed.
Whether normalization belongs in the production watcher or only the test fixture is not established.
No upstream defect or application data loss is claimed.
The watched source files have no changes between the replay revision and the current checkout when inspected.

## Required investigation

Reproduce this exact test on macOS with raw watcher events and fixture canonical paths retained.
Establish the intended identity contract between the watched root and returned paths,
then verify a fix through that boundary and preserve replacement-by-rename coverage.
The separate burst-write and in-place-write assertions also failed in this run;
they are recorded separately until a shared cause is proven.
Missing Clippy and nextest fail-fast are separate harness issues.
